blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The AI use cases that actually work in practice tend to share three things. First, there is a lot of available data for the system to learn from. Second, there is a clear definition of success — 'right or wrong' rather than 'good or bad'. Third, there is a human in the loop at the start, checking and correcting the output, until the system slowly earns its own trust.

The classic examples all look modest. Flagging unusual transactions for a person to review. Translating routine documents. Suggesting draft responses that someone then polishes. Routing incoming customer requests to the right team. Each of these gives the AI a narrow job, a clear signal of success, and an easy fallback to a human whenever confidence is low.

The team we worked with last year said the secret of their AI success was doing 'boring, specific and small'. They meant it as a compliment. At this stage, 'boring, specific and small' is almost always the correct strategy.

items.q: According to the text, what kind of success definition do the working use cases rely on?
items.why: "a clear definition of success — 'right or wrong' rather than 'good or bad'."

items.q: What is the role of the human in the loop at the start?
options: To check and correct the output until the system earns trust
items.why: "a human in the loop at the start, checking and correcting the output, until the system slowly earns its own trust."

items.q: Which feature do all four classic examples share?
options: A fully automated decision with no oversight
A long list of possible outcomes
A narrow job with an easy fallback to a human
items.why: "Each of these gives the AI a narrow job… and an easy fallback to a human whenever confidence is low."

items.q: Why did the team describe 'boring, specific and small' as a COMPLIMENT?
options: Because those qualities are what made the AI work in practice
Because they wanted to sound modest to the board
Because small projects are cheaper to cancel
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata essas qualidades como a fórmula do sucesso — daí ser um elogio, não uma crítica.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The most ambitious, wide-ranging AI project is usually the safest first bet.
A clear signal of success helps an AI use case succeed.
Modest-looking use cases can deliver real value.
A human fallback is valuable when confidence is low.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende 'boring, specific and small' — o oposto de apostar no projeto mais amplo e ambicioso primeiro.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James ajudando a equipe a escolher o primeiro projeto de IA. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so we have twenty ideas on this list, and honestly, most of them are far too ambitious for a first project. I want us to apply one filter, and one filter only: boring, specific and small. If an idea does not pass that test, it goes to the bottom of the pile for now.

Take idea number four — 'an AI that manages the whole trading strategy'. Exciting, yes, but there is no clear right-or-wrong signal, and no easy way for a person to step in when it is unsure. That is exactly the kind of thing that looks impressive in a slide and quietly fails in production.

Now look at idea eleven — flagging unusual transactions for a human to review. It is narrow, we have five years of data for it, and when the model is not confident, a person simply takes over. It will not win any awards, but it will actually work.

So my recommendation is that we start there. Prove the pattern on something small, earn some trust, and then we can be braver next time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What single filter does James want the team to apply to the list of ideas?
items.why: "I want us to apply one filter, and one filter only: boring, specific and small."

items.q: Why does James reject idea number four?
options: The data for it does not exist yet
It is too expensive to build
It has no clear right-or-wrong signal and no easy human fallback
The board has already rejected it
items.why: "there is no clear right-or-wrong signal, and no easy way for a person to step in when it is unsure."

items.q: What makes idea eleven a good first project, according to James?
options: It requires no human involvement at all
It is the most profitable idea on the list
It will win the team an award
It is narrow, has five years of data, and lets a person take over when the model is unsure
items.why: "It is narrow, we have five years of data for it, and when the model is not confident, a person simply takes over."

items.q: What does James imply about ideas that 'look impressive in a slide'?
options: They are easy to demonstrate to clients
They are usually the ones that get funded
They are the safest place to start
They tend to fail quietly once they reach production
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que esse tipo de coisa 'looks impressive in a slide and quietly fails in production' — impressiona, mas falha.

items.q: What is James's overall strategy for the team's AI adoption?
options: Start big to make an impact, then scale down if it fails
Prove the pattern on something small, earn trust, then be braver
Avoid AI until the data is perfect
Let each department choose its own project independently
items.why: Inferência: "Prove the pattern on something small, earn some trust, and then we can be braver next time."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Fraud detection is a strong use case for machine learning." A use case is…
options: a specific situation where a tool delivers value
items.why: Use case = caso de uso: uma situação concreta em que a ferramenta gera valor.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The model performed poorly because there was not enough ___ to learn from."
items.why: Available data = dados disponíveis, aquilo de que o modelo aprende.

items.q: "The system will flag any transaction that looks unusual." To flag something means to…
options: mark it for attention or review
items.why: To flag = sinalizar, marcar algo para que alguém preste atenção ou revise.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When the model is unsure, it hands the case to a person — that human ___ keeps errors under control."
items.why: Fallback = alternativa/plano B: recorrer ao humano quando a confiança é baixa.

items.q: "The chatbot suggests a draft response that an agent then edits." A draft response is…
options: a preliminary version meant to be polished
items.why: Draft response = resposta preliminar, uma primeira versão que a pessoa depois ajusta.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre projetos de IA. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's not bite off more than we can chew with the first project." This means we should not…
options: spend the whole budget at once
take on more than we can realistically handle
items.why: Bite off more than you can chew = assumir mais do que se consegue dar conta.

items.q: "We'll roll out the transaction-flagging tool one desk at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, aos poucos.

items.q: "Before we scale it, the compliance team has to sign off on the model." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "A tiny pilot won't move the needle on revenue, but it proves the pattern." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, no faturamento.

items.q: "The team approved the pilot but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.
